The Survey Events page builds and reuses a DEM for each assigned Stream. One
DEMs card contains Stream-named tabs and maps. Selecting a tab changes the viewed
result; the saved Event inputs determine which work runs.

## Event queue

`survey_event_settings_server()` supplies saved context to
`survey_event_dems_server()`. The latter runs one `terrain_dem_trial_job()` at a
time, using the [input request](dev-11-dem-inputs.html) for the active Stream.
[Mask readiness](dev-12-event-masks.html) is a dependency. Matching saved editions
are reused. Completion or failure advances the queue to the next Stream.

Processing messages identify the Stream being built. Failures retain their
explanation. Pause stops unfinished work while retaining completed results;
Resume retries unfinished Streams. Waiting and Ready are internal queue states.
The analyst guide describes the controls; this chapter describes their execution.

## Transformation planning

The bounded execution qualification in fluvgeo's
`test_terrain_selected_operation_execution.R` verifies an exact catalog
unit-conversion pipeline on a small real DEM window. Direct GDAL output can
retain the source band-unit label after changing elevations. A file-backed
warped VRT followed by explicit target CRS/unit metadata at final GeoTIFF
materialization resolves that mismatch. This does not qualify datum-shift or
coupled-operation execution; saved plans are not yet connected to DEM workers.

Survey Events automatically checks datum compatibility and displays **Datum
transformations** only for pairs requiring a choice. Matching horizontal and
vertical datums hide the controls, including projection or unit differences;
distinct datum realizations still require review. Candidate review uses the
saved Survey Event context in the whole app, before mask and DEM preparation.
A brief checking message is displayed while discovery runs. It uses the
saved source files, Study reference targets and analysis area; no source or target
picker duplicates saved choices. `terrain_transform_review_server()` runs backend
`review_terrain_transformations()` in a worker. One complete operation is chosen
per distinct reference pair, with no default even for a sole available candidate.
Missing-resource, ballpark and epoch-dependent operations remain visible with
reasons but cannot be selected. Descriptions retain combined horizontal/vertical
steps; the analyst does not assemble arbitrary independent pipelines.

`study_transform_store()` saves immutable local JSON plans after rechecking the
input binding and resource/catalog evidence. The plan retains complete candidate
evidence, exact selected pipelines and prior revisions. Reopening restores only
matching choices. These plans do not yet drive DEM execution; the same-CRS worker
below remains unchanged. No datum choice is invented for matching references or
the existing NAVD88 unit conversion. See the analyst guide for the controls and
`dev/schemas/terrain-transform-plan.md` for the persistence contract.

| Function | Data read or written | Ownership and representation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `transform_request()` | Saved source selections/receipts, targets and boundary | Reads Study/Event GeoPackages and original GeoTIFF paths |
| `review_terrain_transformations()` | Embedded source references, local operation catalog/resources | Returns metadata only; no raster writes |
| `save_transform_plan()` / `transform_plan()` | Candidate evidence and explicit selections | Immutable JSON under the Study, bound to its Survey Event; local planning asset |

## Raster calculation

`launch_terrain_dem_trial()` runs these fluvgeo operations in one background worker:

| Operation | Function | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Join consecutive compatible tiles, bilinearly resample each source grid, then merge in priority order | `mosaic_terrain_tiles(template=...)` | First-valid surface on the Event grid |
| Apply the saved Stream domain | `mask_terrain_mosaic()` | DEM on the saved mask grid |
| Convert NAVD88 metres to international feet | `terrain_to_international_feet()` | Float32 DEM with vertical EPSG:8228 |

The worker opens input paths as file-backed terra rasters. Crops restrict work to
the requested extent plus interpolation support, merge preserves first-valid precedence,
bilinear resampling uses the saved mask's geometry, and subsequent masking retains
NoData outside the analysis domain. Unit conversion divides metre elevations by
0.3048 and preserves the horizontal grid and NoData. Outputs use filesystem
GeoTIFFs. Original sources are retained.

The integrated pipeline accepts differing source cell sizes/alignment, with the
same full source CRS/units, the Event's horizontal CRS, and NAVD88 metre elevations.
Consecutive compatible tiles are joined before resampling. Source-grid runs are
resampled to the same full Event template, then combined in saved first/last-valid
order without averaging overlaps. Interleaved source priorities are not reordered.
Runs outside the output extent are omitted; newly adjacent compatible runs are
joined so an irrelevant input cannot split a contributing tile seam.
A two-cell halo at the larger source/output spacing preserves
bilinear support before masking. Source compound CRS and band units are retained;
there is no datum transformation. Cross-CRS processing
and other vertical operations need explicit integration; the
standalone warp API is described under
[terrain developer tools](terrain-developer-tools.html#horizontal-warp-api).

## Completion and display

The job checks the current input binding and recipe before publishing; full
Stream output dimensions/alignment must match the saved mask. Edits, a changed
Event or session closure stop pending work before owned staging cleanup.
[Saved DEM editions](dev-14-dem-editions.html) explains publication and reuse.

Each tab mounts `terrain_mosaic_trial_server(process=FALSE)` as a display-only
module. Lookup is filtered by Stream and scope. The plot uses a bounded display
sample while the analytical GeoTIFF retains its full resolution. The map shows
elevation units, analysis boundary, source tile boundaries and NoData. Optional
DEM details group output/source cell spacing, resampling, storage, method and
timing metadata. Legacy aligned editions retain their original method label and
are reused when their full saved-input recipe still matches. Earlier single-grid
bilinear editions also remain reusable. Mixed-grid details list the input cell
spacings and identify resampling from differing source grids.

## Implementation and tests

Trace `R/survey_event_dems.R`, `R/terrain_dem_trial.R` and
`R/terrain_mosaic_trial.R`. The queue/job tests cover serial dispatch, reuse,
failure retention, cancellation and resume; display tests cover Event-bound
results. Scientific raster tests belong to fluvgeo's terrain-tile-mosaic contract.

Use small actual downloaded DEM windows for development. The mosaic feature record
contains representative full-Stream verification evidence and remaining design
questions. Developer targets and diagnostic fixtures are described in the separate
tools reference rather than used as inputs to the analyst workflow.

## Data objects and storage

See [Data objects and local storage](storage-model.html) for the FGDB ownership and physical representation crosswalk.

| Operation | Data object read or changed | Physical representation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mosaic_terrain_tiles(template=...)` | Combines and resamples differing source grids to the Event grid | Reads source GeoTIFFs and mask geometry; writes one mosaic GeoTIFF; transient source-grid/run rasters are removed |
| `mask_terrain_mosaic()` | Restricts the mosaic to the saved analysis domain | Reads mosaic/mask GeoTIFFs; writes masked DEM GeoTIFF |
| `terrain_to_international_feet()` | Converts supported elevation units | Writes Float32 GeoTIFF with vertical reference evidence |
| Stream result display | Reads assembled terrain associated with the selected Stream and acquisition definition | External GeoTIFF; no governed feature-class update |

The intended design keeps DEM processing at Stream scale; Reaches reference the applicable edition and apply their analysis domains. This pipeline does not perform
hydro-modification or create the governed Reach Survey Event hydro DEM. Shared
Stream terrain can support several later Reach/Event products through explicit
asset associations; it must not be assigned a fictitious single Event owner.
